_note: Original items authored for EduNexus, written to the Digital SAT taxonomy in CLAUDE.md section 5. Not College Board content.

questions.stimulus: The results of the experiment ______ published in a journal last spring.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The subject is 'results,' which is plural, so the verb must be plural and in the past tense to match 'last spring.' 'Were' is correct; the other options are singular.

questions.stimulus: The storm knocked out power to the entire district ______ classes were canceled for two days.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Both halves are independent clauses, so joining them requires a comma plus a coordinating conjunction. A comma alone creates a comma splice, and the remaining options run the clauses together.

questions.stimulus: Each of the participants ______ asked to complete a short questionnaire before the session began.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The subject is 'Each,' a singular pronoun; 'of the participants' is a prepositional phrase that does not change the subject's number. The past-tense singular 'was' is correct.

questions.stimulus: After finishing her degree in marine biology ______ Ortiz spent two years studying coral reefs in the Philippines.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The opening phrase is an introductory modifier, not an independent clause, so it is set off with a comma. Semicolons and colons require what precedes them to be an independent clause.

questions.stimulus: The library extended ______ hours during the examination period.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: A possessive pronoun is needed for the singular 'library.' 'Its' is that possessive; 'it's' means 'it is,' 'its'' is not a word, and 'their' is plural.

questions.stimulus: The recipe calls for three ingredients ______ flour, butter, and salt.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: A colon introduces a list after an independent clause, which 'The recipe calls for three ingredients' is. A semicolon would require an independent clause after it, and the other options produce a run-on.

questions.stimulus: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers ______ shelter under an overhang.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The sheltering happened before the team's arrival, and both are in the past, so the past perfect 'had taken' is required to mark the earlier action.

questions.stimulus: Kenji studied architecture in Osaka ______ he now designs public libraries.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Two independent clauses may be joined by a semicolon. A comma alone creates a splice, 'and,' misplaces the comma, and omitting punctuation creates a run-on.

questions.stimulus: The committee, along with several outside consultants, ______ scheduled to review the proposal next month.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The subject is the singular 'committee.' A phrase beginning 'along with' is parenthetical and does not make the subject plural, so the singular 'is' agrees, matching the future reference in 'next month.'

questions.stimulus: The novel's first edition ______ printed in 1847 and now extremely rare ______ sold at auction for a record sum.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: 'Printed in 1847 and now extremely rare' is a nonessential modifier interrupting the subject and verb, so it must be set off with a matching pair of commas. Using only one comma leaves the interruption unclosed, and semicolons cannot enclose a phrase.

questions.stimulus: Neither the director nor the producers ______ willing to comment on the delay.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: In a 'neither...nor' construction, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural 'producers.' The plural past-tense 'were' is correct.

questions.stimulus: The technique has one significant drawback ______ it cannot be used on samples smaller than a cubic centimeter.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The first clause is independent and the second explains the drawback it announces, which is exactly what a colon signals. A comma alone would splice two independent clauses, and 'and' would obscure the explanatory relationship.

questions.stimulus: Having reviewed the data for several weeks, ______
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: the conclusion was revised by the researchers.
it was decided that the conclusion should be revised.
there was a revision of the conclusion.

questions.rationale: The introductory participial phrase must modify whoever did the reviewing. Only C places 'the researchers' immediately after it; the other options leave the modifier dangling, implying the conclusion or an unnamed subject did the reviewing.

questions.stimulus: Marie Tharp mapped the ocean floor for decades ______ her work revealed the mid-Atlantic ridge and helped confirm plate tectonics.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Two independent clauses in an additive relationship need a comma plus a coordinating conjunction. 'And' fits the relationship; 'however' after only a comma creates a splice, 'but' signals a contrast that is not present, and a bare comma splices.

questions.stimulus: The number of applications the office receives each spring ______ risen sharply since the program was expanded.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The subject is 'The number,' which is singular; 'of applications the office receives each spring' modifies it without changing its number. The singular 'has' is correct.

questions.stimulus: The vessel carried cargo from three ports ______ Lisbon, Portugal ______ Valencia, Spain ______ and Genoa, Italy.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: A colon introduces the list after the independent clause, and because each item already contains a comma separating city from country, semicolons must separate the items to keep them distinct.

questions.stimulus: The archive holds letters from dozens of correspondents, many of ______ were never identified by name.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The pronoun is the object of the preposition 'of,' which requires the objective form 'whom.' 'Who' is subjective, 'which' cannot refer to people, and 'them' would leave the clause without a relative pronoun, creating a splice.

questions.stimulus: Researchers had expected the compound to degrade within hours ______ instead, it remained stable for more than three weeks under identical conditions.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Both clauses are independent, and 'instead' is a conjunctive adverb rather than a coordinating conjunction, so a semicolon is required before it. A comma alone would create a splice.

questions.stimulus: The survey found that residents of the coastal districts were more likely to support the levy than ______
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: residents of the inland districts were.

questions.rationale: The comparison is between two groups of residents, so both terms must be parallel. Choice B compares residents to residents. Choice A compares residents to districts, C is not a comparable term, and D introduces a singular pronoun with no matching antecedent.

questions.stimulus: The 1906 earthquake destroyed much of the city ______ rebuilding began almost immediately, and within a decade the population had surpassed its pre-disaster peak.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: Two independent clauses in a contrastive relationship require a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, and 'but' supplies both. 'Nevertheless' and 'however' are conjunctive adverbs that cannot join clauses with only a comma, and a bare comma splices.

questions.stimulus: Neither of the two proposed routes ______ without significant drawbacks, according to the engineers who evaluated them.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: 'Neither' functions as a singular subject, and 'of the two proposed routes' is a prepositional phrase that does not affect agreement. The singular 'is' is correct.

questions.stimulus: The composer Ethel Smyth ______ whose opera *The Wreckers* premiered in Leipzig in 1906 ______ was also active in the campaign for women's suffrage.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The relative clause beginning 'whose' is nonessential, since the composer is already identified by name, so it takes a matching pair of commas. Omitting either comma leaves the interruption unbalanced, and a colon cannot open a nonessential clause.

questions.stimulus: If the sample ______ contaminated during transport, the entire analysis would have to be repeated.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The main clause uses 'would have to be,' which signals a hypothetical condition and calls for the subjunctive in the 'if' clause. 'Were to be' supplies it; the indicative forms do not match the conditional main clause.

questions.stimulus: The new telescope will allow astronomers to observe fainter objects, map distant galaxies, and ______ the composition of exoplanet atmospheres.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.rationale: The series follows 'to' once: 'to observe, map, and determine.' Parallel structure requires the bare infinitive form to match 'observe' and 'map,' so 'determine' is correct.
